questions.question: What is RuboCop and how do you use it?
questions.title: RuboCop Basics
questions.direct_answer: RuboCop is Ruby's linter/formatter: it enforces the Ruby Style Guide and catches smells. Install (gem install rubocop), run `rubocop` in your project — it lists offenses (style, complexity, naming) with file:line and a cop name. Auto-correct with `rubocop -a` (safe fixes) or `rubocop -A` (all safe + unsafe). Configure with .rubocop.yml (enable/disable cops, set target Ruby version, excludes). Cops are grouped: Style (formatting), Layout (spacing), Metrics (complexity/length), Naming, Lint (bugs). In Rails, rubocop-rails adds Rails-specific cops. Use it to keep code consistent and catch issues early, but don't blindly auto-correct everything — review the diffs. Run it in CI to prevent style drift.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know RuboCop is a linter/formatter, you run `rubocop`, auto-correct with -a, and configure with .rubocop.yml.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Blindly running rubocop -A (it can change semantics), or disabling cops to silence warnings instead of fixing the code.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: RuboCop lints/formats Ruby. Run `rubocop`; -a auto-corrects safe; -A all safe+unsafe. Configure with .rubocop.yml. Cops: Style/Layout/Metrics/Naming/Lint; rubocop-rails for Rails.

sections.title: RuboCop
sections.content:
```ruby
# Install:  gem install rubocop   (rubocop-rails for Rails)
# Run in your project:
#   rubocop                 # list offenses (file:line + cop name)
#   rubocop -a              # auto-correct SAFE fixes
#   rubocop -A              # auto-correct safe AND unsafe (review!)

# Example output:
#   app/models/post.rb:15:3: C: Style/GuardClause: Replace ... with a guard clause.
#   app/controllers/posts_controller.rb:7:5: C: Metrics/MethodLength: Method has 20 lines.

# .rubocop.yml (configure):
AllCops:
  NewCops: enable
  TargetRubyVersion: 3.2
Style/Documentation:
  Enabled: false            # disable a cop
Metrics/MethodLength:
  Max: 20                  # raise a threshold
Exclude:
  - 'db/schema.rb'

# Cop groups: Style (formatting), Layout (spacing), Metrics (complexity),
#             Naming, Lint (bugs). rubocop-rails adds Rails-specific cops.
# Run in CI to prevent style drift. Don't blindly -A; review the diffs.
```
